# Prepare Survey Data

## L2 variables

```{r}
## =====================================================================
## Per-scale validation via CFAstats() + composite descriptives
## Loops your CFAstats() wrapper over every scale, then computes the
## scale-score mean_<short> / SD_<short> objects (e.g. mean_cmq, SD_cmq).
##
## Requires in scope:
##   - stringr, psych, lavaan, semPlot, moments, ggplot2/dplyr/tidyr/forcats
##   - your helpers: CFAstats(), getDescriptivesSurvey(), model_lavaan(),
##     dimensionalityTest(), explorativeFactorAnalysis()
##   - the data frame `ques_study`
## =====================================================================

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Scale definitions
##    - list name   = suffix for mean_<name> / SD_<name>
##    - labelLatent = passed to CFAstats(); also used as the lavaan latent
##                    variable name, so it MUST be a valid identifier
##                    (no spaces, no "-"). CFAstats strips "-" from the
##                    *item* names/regex itself, so keep "-" in regEx.
##    - regEx       = column selector (matches the ORIGINAL column names)
##    The ^ anchor stops "^utopianism" from catching "anti_utopianism".
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
scaleConfig <- list(
  activism   = list(labelLatent = "ARIS_Activism",               regEx = "^aris_scale-ais"),
  radicalism = list(labelLatent = "ARIS_Radicalism",             regEx = "^aris_scale-ris"),
  utop       = list(labelLatent = "Utopianism",                  regEx = "^utopianism_scale-utop"),
  antiutop   = list(labelLatent = "AntiUtopianism",              regEx = "^anti_utopianism_scale-antiutop"),
  nfc        = list(labelLatent = "NeedForChaos",                regEx = "^nfc_scale-nfc"),
  sjs        = list(labelLatent = "SystemJustification",         regEx = "^sjs_scale-sjs"),
  swls       = list(labelLatent = "SatisfactionWithLife",        regEx = "^swls_scale-swls"),
  brs        = list(labelLatent = "BriefResilience",             regEx = "^brs_scale-brs"),
  prds       = list(labelLatent = "PersonalRelativeDeprivation", regEx = "^prds_scale-prds"),
  cmq        = list(labelLatent = "ConspiracyMentality",         regEx = "^cmq_scale-cmq")
)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1b. Reverse-code the reverse-keyed (…r) items  --  RUN ONCE
##     Formula (as requested): reversed = max(item) - item, using each
##     item's own (empirical) maximum.
##     Applied to the global ques_study BEFORE CFAstats() and the
##     composites, so EFA/CFA loadings come out positive and the scale
##     means are correct.
##     Guarded against accidental re-running (re-flipping would corrupt
##     the values) -- reload ques_study fresh if you need to redo it.
##     Note: max(item) - item puts the reversed items on a 0..(max-min)
##     range. To keep them on the original min..max scale instead, use
##     (min(item) + max(item)) - item.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
revCols <- c("sjs_scale-sjs3r", "sjs_scale-sjs7r",
             "brs_scale-brs2r", "brs_scale-brs4r", "brs_scale-brs6r",
             "prds_scale-prds2r", "prds_scale-prds4r")

if (!exists("reverseCodingDone") || !isTRUE(reverseCodingDone)) {
  for (col in revCols) {
    ques_study_wide[[col]] <- max(ques_study_wide[[col]], na.rm = TRUE) - ques_study_wide[[col]]
  }
  reverseCodingDone <- TRUE
  message("Reverse-coded (max - item): ", paste(revCols, collapse = ", "))
} else {
  message("Reverse coding already applied; skipping. Reload ques_study_wide to redo.")
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Run CFAstats() for every scale
##    Toggle the components once here; they apply to all scales.
##    NB: CFAstats() runs the EFA as a fixed 1-factor solution and the
##        CFA as a 1-factor (unidimensional) lavaan model.
##        Mplus is OFF (needs Mplus installed; latent name must be <=8
##        chars for Mplus -- shorten labelLatent above if you enable it).
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
opt_showPlots       <- TRUE   # cor.plot + getDescriptivesSurvey()
opt_computeEFA      <- TRUE   # dimensionalityTest() + 1-factor EFA
opt_computeCFA      <- TRUE   # lavaan 1-factor CFA (MLR) + semPaths + MIs
opt_computeCFAMplus <- FALSE  # Mplus CFA + McDonald's omega

cfaResults <- list()
for (short in names(scaleConfig)) {
  cfg <- scaleConfig[[short]]
  cat("\n\n===================== ", cfg$labelLatent, " =====================\n")

  cfaResults[[short]] <- CFAstats(
    dataset         = ques_study_wide,
    regularExp      = cfg$regEx,
    labelLatent     = cfg$labelLatent,
    showPlots       = opt_showPlots,
    computeEFA      = opt_computeEFA,
    computeCFA      = opt_computeCFA,
    computeCFAMplus = opt_computeCFAMplus
  )
}
## inspect later, e.g.:
##   cfaResults$cmq$EFA[[1]]$loadings
##   cfaResults$cmq$cronbachAlpha$total$raw_alpha
##   summary(cfaResults$cmq$CFA, fit.measures = TRUE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Per-participant scale scores -> bind as new columns to ques_study_wide
##    For every scale and every participant (row), ONE value each:
##      mean_<short> = row mean across the scale's items   (na.rm = TRUE)
##      sd_<short>   = row SD   across the scale's items    (na.rm = TRUE)
##    sd_<short> captures within-person spread across that scale's items.
##    Reverse coding (step 1b) is already applied to ques_study_wide, so the
##    items are correctly oriented here.
##    (For large data, apply(.,1,sd) can be replaced by matrixStats::rowSds.)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
for (short in names(scaleConfig)) {
  cfg   <- scaleConfig[[short]]
  sel   <- str_detect(colnames(ques_study_wide), cfg$regEx)
  items <- as.matrix(ques_study_wide[, sel])

  ques_study_wide[[paste0("mean_", short)]] <- rowMeans(items, na.rm = TRUE)
  ques_study_wide[[paste0("sd_",   short)]] <- apply(items, 1L, sd, na.rm = TRUE)
}

## peek at the new columns
head(ques_study_wide[, grep("^(mean|sd)_", colnames(ques_study_wide)), drop = FALSE])

## OPTIONAL: sample-level summary (mean & SD ACROSS participants of each
## scale's mean score) -- the earlier mean_<short>/SD_<short> table.
descriptives <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(scaleConfig), function(short) {
  sc <- ques_study_wide[[paste0("mean_", short)]]
  data.frame(scale   = scaleConfig[[short]]$labelLatent,
             mean    = mean(sc, na.rm = TRUE),
             sd      = sd(sc,   na.rm = TRUE),
             n_items = sum(str_detect(colnames(ques_study_wide),
                                      scaleConfig[[short]]$regEx)))
}))
descriptives
```


```{r}
########################################
# correlation plot of all scale means
########################################
corPlotMeans <- function(dataset, pattern = "^mean_", main = "Scale means") {
  sel <- stringr::str_detect(colnames(dataset), pattern)
  m   <- dataset[, sel, drop = FALSE]
  colnames(m) <- sub(pattern, "", colnames(m))      # drop "mean_" for cleaner labels
  tmp_cor <- cor(m, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  psych::cor.plot(r = tmp_cor, upper = FALSE, xlas = 2, main = main)
  invisible(tmp_cor)                                # returns the matrix too
}

corPlotMeans(ques_study_wide)
```



## L1 variables


```{r}
## =====================================================================
## Within-vignettes analysis (long -> per-row composites -> wide EFA)
## Data: ques_study_within_vignettes
##   one row per participant x vignette; 7 vignettes (condition_FutureSociety)
##   per PROLIFIC_PID. No reverse coding needed.
## Requires: stringr, psych, dplyr, tidyr
##   (+ your helpers CFAstats(), dimensionalityTest(),
##      explorativeFactorAnalysis() if you run the optional item-level part)
## =====================================================================


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 0. Items are stored as <chr> -> convert to numeric
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
itemCols <- c("pe1", "pe2", "pe3", "pe4",
              "att_ideal", "att_beneficial", "att_utopian",
              "att_desirable", "att_innovative", "att_live_in")

ques_study_within_vignettes[itemCols] <-
  lapply(ques_study_within_vignettes[itemCols], as.numeric)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Scale definitions (no reverse items here)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
scaleConfigWithin <- list(
  pe  = list(labelLatent = "PE",  regEx = "^pe[0-9]+$"),  # pe1..pe4
  att = list(labelLatent = "ATT", regEx = "^att_")        # the 6 att_* items
)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. (OPTIONAL) item-level validation via CFAstats(), same as before.
##    pe/att items are ordered Likert, so polychoric (the helper's
##    non-"Overall" path) is appropriate here.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# cfaResultsWithin <- list()
# for (short in names(scaleConfigWithin)) {
#   cfg <- scaleConfigWithin[[short]]
#   cat("\n\n===================== ", cfg$labelLatent, " =====================\n")
#   cfaResultsWithin[[short]] <- CFAstats(
#     dataset = as.data.frame(ques_study_within_vignettes),
#     regularExp = cfg$regEx, labelLatent = cfg$labelLatent,
#     showPlots = TRUE, computeEFA = TRUE, computeCFA = TRUE, computeCFAMplus = FALSE)
# }

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Per-participant-per-vignette composites -> bind to the long data
##    mean_<short> = row mean across the scale's items   (na.rm = TRUE)
##    sd_<short>   = row SD   across the scale's items    (na.rm = TRUE)
##    -> one value per row (participant x vignette).
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
for (short in names(scaleConfigWithin)) {
  cfg   <- scaleConfigWithin[[short]]
  sel   <- str_detect(colnames(ques_study_within_vignettes), cfg$regEx)
  items <- as.matrix(ques_study_within_vignettes[, sel])

  ques_study_within_vignettes[[paste0("mean_", short)]] <- rowMeans(items, na.rm = TRUE)
  ques_study_within_vignettes[[paste0("sd_",   short)]] <- apply(items, 1L, sd, na.rm = TRUE)
}

head(ques_study_within_vignettes[, grep("^(mean|sd)_(pe|att)$",
                                         colnames(ques_study_within_vignettes)),
                                  drop = FALSE])

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Reshape to WIDE: one row per PROLIFIC_PID, one column per society.
##    Cell = that participant's composite score for that society.
##    values_fn guards against a participant seeing a society >1 time.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
makeWide <- function(data, valueCol,
                     idCol  = "PROLIFIC_PID",
                     keyCol = "condition_FutureSociety") {
  data %>%
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(idCol, keyCol, valueCol))) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(
      id_cols     = dplyr::all_of(idCol),
      names_from  = dplyr::all_of(keyCol),
      values_from = dplyr::all_of(valueCol),
      values_fn   = function(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Correlation plot + parallel analysis + EFA on the wide matrix.
##    Composites are continuous, so use Pearson (not polychoric).
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
corEFAwide <- function(wide, idCol = "PROLIFIC_PID", label = "wide") {
  m <- as.data.frame(wide[, setdiff(colnames(wide), idCol), drop = FALSE])

  ## correlation heat-map across the 7 societies
  tmp_cor <- cor(m, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  psych::cor.plot(r = tmp_cor, upper = FALSE, xlas = 2, main = label)

  ## parallel analysis -> suggested number of factors
  pa <- psych::fa.parallel(m, fm = "minres", fa = "both", main = label, cor = "cor")
  nf <- max(1, pa$nfact)

  ## EFA
  efa <- psych::fa(r = tmp_cor, nfactors = nf,
                   rotate = if (nf > 1) "promax" else "none",
                   n.obs = nrow(m))
  cat("\n", label, " - EFA loadings (", nf, " factor(s)):\n", sep = "")
  print(efa$loadings)

  list(cor = tmp_cor, parallel = pa, nfact = nf, efa = efa)
}

## build wide data + run, for each composite
wide_pe  <- makeWide(ques_study_within_vignettes, "mean_pe")
wide_att <- makeWide(ques_study_within_vignettes, "mean_att")

res_pe_wide  <- corEFAwide(wide_pe,  label = "PE across societies")
res_att_wide <- corEFAwide(wide_att, label = "ATT across societies")

## inspect later, e.g. res_att_wide$efa$loadings ; res_att_wide$nfact
```

# k means

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# Merge Participative Efficacy + Attribute scores and cluster participants
# with k-means using the mlr3 / mlr3cluster framework.
# =============================================================================

# ---- Packages ---------------------------------------------------------------
# install.packages(c("dplyr", "mlr3", "mlr3cluster", "mlr3pipelines"))
library(dplyr)
library(mlr3)
library(mlr3cluster)
library(mlr3pipelines)

set.seed(42)  # reproducibility (k-means uses random starts)

# ---- 1. Merge the two wide data sets ----------------------------------------
# Both tibbles share the same 7 utopia column names, so we suffix them
# (_pe = Participative Efficacy, _att = Attributes) before joining on the ID.
pe  <- wide_pe  %>% rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_pe"),  .cols = -PROLIFIC_PID)
att <- wide_att %>% rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_att"), .cols = -PROLIFIC_PID)

merged <- inner_join(pe, att, by = "PROLIFIC_PID")

merged <- att 

# Sanity checks: k-means cannot handle missing values, and the join should
# keep all participants present in both tables.
cat("Rows after merge:", nrow(merged), "\n")          # expect 486
cat("Missing values  :", sum(is.na(merged)), "\n")    # must be 0
# If NAs exist, decide how to handle them, e.g.:
merged <- tidyr::drop_na(merged)

# ---- 2. Build the clustering task (drop the ID column) ----------------------
# The PROLIFIC_PID is an identifier, not a feature, so it is excluded.
feat <- merged %>% select(-PROLIFIC_PID)
task <- as_task_clust(feat)

# ---- 3. Choose the number of clusters (silhouette sweep) --------------------
# Average silhouette width: higher = better-separated clusters.
k_grid <- 2:12
sil <- vapply(k_grid, function(kk) {
  gl <- as_learner(
    po("scale") %>>% lrn("clust.kmeans", centers = kk,
                         algorithm = "Lloyd", nstart = 25, iter.max = 100)
  )
  gl$train(task)
  gl$predict(task)$score(msr("clust.silhouette"), task = task)
}, numeric(1))

k_selection <- data.frame(k = k_grid, silhouette = round(sil, 4))
print(k_selection)
best_k <- 7 # k_grid[which.max(sil)]
cat("Best k by silhouette:", best_k, "\n")

# ---- 4. Fit the final k-means model -----------------------------------------
# Set k to the value you decide on (here: the silhouette-optimal one; replace
# with a substantively justified number, e.g. k <- 3, if you prefer).
k <- best_k

final_learner <- as_learner(
  po("scale") %>>%
  lrn("clust.kmeans", centers = k, algorithm = "Lloyd",
      nstart = 25, iter.max = 100)
)
final_learner$train(task)

# ---- 5. Assign the most likely class to every participant -------------------
pred <- final_learner$predict(task)
merged$cluster <- pred$partition          # integer cluster label per row

result <- merged %>% select(PROLIFIC_PID, cluster)
print(head(result, 10))

# Cluster sizes
print(table(merged$cluster))

# ---- 6. (Optional) Inspect cluster profiles ---------------------------------
# Mean feature values per cluster help you interpret/label the clusters.
profiles <- merged %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  summarise(across(-PROLIFIC_PID, ~ round(mean(.x), 2)), .groups = "drop")
print(profiles)
```

# Merge cluster labels onto the full questionnaire data
ques_clustered <- ques_study_wide %>%
  left_join(result, by = "PROLIFIC_PID")   # result = PROLIFIC_PID + cluster

# Aggregate the mean_* variables per cluster
mean_vars <- c("mean_activism", "mean_radicalism", "mean_utop", "mean_antiutop",
               "mean_nfc", "mean_sjs", "mean_swls", "mean_brs",
               "mean_prds") # , "mean_cmq"

mean_profiles_long <- ques_clustered %>%
  filter(!is.na(cluster)) %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(mean_vars), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(-cluster, names_to = "variable", values_to = "mean") %>%
  mutate(cluster  = factor(cluster),
         variable = sub("^mean_", "", variable))   # tidy labels

ggplot(mean_profiles_long, aes(x = variable, y = mean,
                               group = cluster, colour = cluster)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean score", colour = "Cluster",
       title = "Mean dispositional/scale variables by cluster") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)
# Cluster labels already merged onto the questionnaire data:
# ques_clustered <- ques_study_wide %>% left_join(result, by = "PROLIFIC_PID")
dat <- ques_clustered %>%
  filter(!is.na(cluster)) %>%
  mutate(cluster = factor(cluster))

mean_vars <- c("mean_activism", "mean_radicalism", "mean_utop", "mean_antiutop",
               "mean_nfc", "mean_sjs", "mean_swls", "mean_brs",
               "mean_prds", "mean_cmq")

# ---- ANOVA per variable -----------------------------------------------------
anova_results <- lapply(mean_vars, function(v) {
  fit <- aov(reformulate("cluster", response = v), data = dat)
  tidy(fit) %>%
    filter(term == "cluster") %>%
    transmute(variable = v, df = df, F = statistic, p = p.value)
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p, method = "holm"),   # correct for 10 tests
         sig   = cut(p_adj, c(-Inf, .001, .01, .05, Inf),
                     labels = c("***", "**", "*", "ns")))

print(anova_results)

# ---- Post-hoc (only for variables that are significant) ---------------------
sig_vars <- anova_results$variable[anova_results$p_adj < .05]
posthoc <- lapply(sig_vars, function(v) {
  TukeyHSD(aov(reformulate("cluster", response = v), data = dat))$cluster %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("contrast") %>%
    mutate(variable = v)
}) %>% bind_rows()
print(posthoc)
```


```{r}
# ---- Simple plot: cluster means for all variables --------------------------

mean_vars <- c(mean_vars, "lrscale", "rlgdgr")
plot_df <- dat %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(mean_vars),
                   list(m  = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                        se = ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(.x)))),
                   .names = "{.col}__{.fn}"),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(-cluster, names_to = c("variable", ".value"), names_sep = "__") %>%
  mutate(variable = sub("^mean_", "", variable))

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = cluster, y = m, fill = cluster)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = m - se, ymax = m + se), width = .3) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Cluster", y = "Mean (± SE)",
       title = "Cluster means by scale variable (one-way ANOVA)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## ranking 



```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Define ranking columns
rank_cols <- c("rank_ai_centered", "rank_primitivist", "rank_institutional", 
               "rank_moral_anarchic", "rank_futurist", "rank_modern_green")

# dat <- dat %>%
#   mutate(across(all_of(rank_cols), ~ 8 - .)) # !!!!!!!

# 2. Reshape to long format
dat_long <- dat %>%
  select(cluster, all_of(rank_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -cluster, names_to = "utopia_type", values_to = "rank") %>%
  mutate(utopia_type = gsub("rank_", "", utopia_type)) 

# 3. Calculate mean rank (lower = better)
mean_ranks <- dat_long %>%
  group_by(cluster, utopia_type) %>%
  summarise(mean_rank = mean(rank, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# 4. Heatmap with reversed color scale 
# Low values (1) are now visually highlighted as the strongest preferences
ggplot(mean_ranks, aes(x = utopia_type, y = as.factor(cluster), fill = mean_rank)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "darkred", high = "white") + 
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Dominance of Utopian Preferences",
    subtitle = "Darker red indicates a lower mean rank (higher preference/closer to 1)",
    x = "Utopian Society Type",
    y = "Cluster ID",
    fill = "Mean Rank"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

grp <- z %>%
  mutate(destructive = ifelse(mean_radicalism < 2 & mean_nfc < 2, "non-violent","other"))
# 4 = scale midpoint => genuine endorsement, not just "less opposed"
table(grp$destructive)

# outcomes NOT used to define the group:
for (v in c("mean_brs","mean_swls","mean_cmq", "mean_antiutop")) {
  cat("\n", v, "\n")
  print(t.test(reformulate("destructive", v), data = grp))   # Welch, unequal var
  print(effectsize::cohens_d(reformulate("destructive", v), data = grp))
}
